objective.value: Design and demonstrate a novel DERA-based synthetic pathway in E. coli that converts formaldehyde (HCHO) and ethanol into 1,3-propanediol (PDO) via aldol condensation of HCHO and acetaldehyde (ACALD) to 3-hydroxypropionaldehyde (3-HPA), implemented as three metabolic modules (ACALD supply, HCHO supply, DERA-based PDO production).
objective.notes: Objective stated in abstract and restated in conclusion.

hypothesis.value: Acetaldehyde (ACALD), not pyruvate, is the real HCHO acceptor in the C-C bond-forming aldol reaction; therefore an aldolase (DERA) may catalyze the direct aldol condensation of HCHO and ACALD to form 3-HPA, which can be reduced to PDO.
hypothesis.notes: Framed by the authors as a question derived from analysis of their previous KHB/pyruvate pathway.

value.host: Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) (fermentation/bioconversion host); E. coli Top10 (cloning only)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: active design choice of a new pathway reaction (DERA-catalyzed HCHO+ACALD condensation). Q2: implemented in this study. Q3: a deliberate pathway design, not a measurement.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Use acetaldehyde (ACALD) as the HCHO acceptor and DERA as the aldolase to form 3-HPA directly, replacing the previous KHB/pyruvate route
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Authors observed that the carboxyl group of pyruvate is not involved in the aldol condensation and is removed afterwards, indicating ACALD is the real HCHO receptor (results_and_discussion_p001).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Prior-work analysis: in the KHB-based pathway the carboxyl group of pyruvate is removed after the condensation step (results_and_discussion_p001); chemical HCHO+ACALD condensation requires >250 °C with side reactions (results_and_discussion_p002).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent + mechanistic reasoning from the authors' own prior pathway; the DERA/ACALD route itself was untested until this work.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The choice is justified by reaction-mechanism analysis of the prior pathway (carboxyl group of pyruvate is superfluous), stated before the experiments.

generalizable_rule.candidate: ACALD can serve as a direct aldol acceptor for HCHO in DERA-catalyzed condensation to form 3-HPA as a PDO precursor.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: E. coli BL21(DE3) whole-cell bioconversion with DERA_ECO/DERA_TMA + DhaT, HCHO 10-100 mM, ACALD 10-100 mM or ethanol 300 mM, 30 °C, pH 7.0
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other hosts, other aldehyde acceptors, in vivo growth-coupled production, industrial scale; not validated beyond the tested conditions

alternatives_considered: pyruvate as acceptor via KHB (previous work; carboxyl carbon lost)
chemical aldol condensation of HCHO and ACALD (>250 °C, severe side reactions)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: enzyme selection is a design choice. Q2: screening performed in this study. Q3: selection of DERA_TMA for the pathway is a decision outcome.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Select DERA from Thermotoga maritima (DERA_TMA) as the pathway aldolase after screening DERAs from heat-resistant bacteria in vivo and in vitro
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: DERA_TMA gave the highest PDO concentration/yield in vivo (8.20 ± 0.04 mM, Table 2) and highest specific activity at 10 mM HCHO (1.27 ± 0.02 U/mg), considering both activity and HCHO tolerance (a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p010).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Need for a more efficient DERA; literature suggestion that heat resistance relates to aldehyde tolerance (results_and_discussion_p006).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=screening_result (experimental measurement in this study, Tables 2 and Figure 5).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Choice made from a direct comparative screen of four to six DERA variants performed by the authors.
alternatives_considered: DERA_ECO, DERA_GTH, DERA_SEP, DERA_PAE (lower in vivo PDO, Table 2)
DERA_ECO C47M/C47V and DERA_Rd3BB (better HCHO tolerance but not adopted for the final strain)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: choice of HpADH1 to build the ACALD supply module. Q2: implemented here (BF12). Q3: deliberate module design decision.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Generate ACALD intracellularly from ethanol using alcohol dehydrogenase HpADH1 from Hansenula polymorpha instead of direct ACALD addition
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Direct ACALD addition is expensive, inconvenient and harmful to the biocatalyst; ethanol oxidation also supplies NADH balance (a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p011).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Cost/operation/toxicity concerns of direct ACALD feeding and the NADH balance issue identified before module construction (a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p011).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent (HpADH1 performance on ethanol, refs 39-40) plus in vitro verification with purified proteins (Figures S1C,D, unavailable) and in vivo improvement (Figure 6C).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: HpADH1 was chosen because literature showed good performance converting ethanol to acetaldehyde; verified in this study.
alternatives_considered: direct ACALD addition (rejected: expensive, inconvenient, harmful)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: targeted gene knockout. Q2: performed in this study via CRISPR-Cas9 (BF16). Q3: deliberate flux-redirection design.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Delete the frmA gene (encoding HCHO dehydrogenase of the frmRAB system) in E. coli BL21(DE3) using CRISPR-Cas9
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: HCHO is converted to formate endogenously, lowering PDO yield; deleting frmA reduces this competing consumption (a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p012/p017).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Relatively low PDO yield from ethanol and HCHO, attributed to HCHO-to-formate conversion as reported in the authors' previous study (a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p012).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement (prior study observation + this study's BF12→BF16 comparison, Figure 6C,D).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The target gene's enzymatic function (HCHO dehydrogenase) and its competition for the pathway substrate are known and stated before/at the design step.

generalizable_rule.candidate: Deleting frmA to block endogenous HCHO-to-formate conversion increases PDO concentration and yield in DERA-based HCHO+ethanol bioconversion.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: E. coli BL21(DE3) pRSFduet-DERA_TMA-HpADH1-DhaT, batch bioconversion 300 mM ethanol / 100 mM HCHO, OD600=50, 30 °C
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other hosts, other HCHO assimilation pathways, growth-coupled conditions; formate formation was not fully eliminated (observed in fed-batch)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: process-level feeding design. Q2: implemented in this study (Figure 8). Q3: deliberate fed-batch design to control HCHO level.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Perform fed-batch bioconversion with interim HCHO additions (100 mM in ten intervals) to keep HCHO above ~0.6 mM
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Diol byproducts form when HCHO is nearly depleted; in vitro data show >0.6 mM HCHO strongly inhibits ACALD self-condensation and its condensation with 3-HPA (a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p019).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Observation in this study that diol byproducts were generated only when HCHO was nearly completely consumed, plus the in vitro HCHO-dependence result (a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p019) - both preceding the fed-batch design.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement (in vitro byproduct-vs-HCHO assay, Figure 7F, and batch observation).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The feeding strategy is directly justified by the measured inhibitory effect of HCHO on the side condensations.

generalizable_rule.candidate: Maintaining HCHO above ~0.6 mM during DERA-based whole-cell bioconversion suppresses diol byproduct formation from ACALD self-condensation and ACALD+3-HPA condensation.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: BF16 resting-cell bioconversion, ethanol 300 mM, HCHO kept >0.6 mM via ten interim additions, 30 °C, pH 7.0; in vitro confirmation with purified enzymes
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other aldolases/hosts, continuously fed or growth-coupled processes; threshold derived only for this system

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: enzyme/module choice for HCHO supply from methanol. Q2: implemented (BF17). Q3: deliberate design, though outcome was poor.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Use methanol dehydrogenase Mdh2 (from B. methanolicus MGA3) to oxidize methanol to HCHO as a HCHO supply module
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Stated aim: develop a HCHO supply module with methanol as substrate (a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p018). No specific reason for choosing Mdh2 over other Mdhs is reported.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Need for a HCHO supply module; methanol considered as substrate (a_in_vivo_dera_assay_p018).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=author_assertion for the selection; outcome measured experimentally (1.05 mM PDO, 42 h; Mdh activity bottleneck, Figure S1E unavailable).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: 理由未报告: the paper states that Mdh2 was selected but gives no explicit selection rationale.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: point-mutation construction. Q2: mutants constructed and tested in this study. Q3: deliberate variant design for aldehyde tolerance testing.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Construct and test DERA_ECO C47M, DERA_ECO C47V and DERA_TMA C65M mutants for aldehyde tolerance
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Literature: ACALD-derived 3-hydroxybutanal forms a covalent bond with C47 of DERA_ECO causing irreversible deactivation; C47M/C47V mutations alleviate it (results_and_discussion_p007, refs 34, 37).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Literature reports of C47-mediated irreversible DERA inactivation by ACALD (background citations, results_and_discussion_p007) - predates the mutant construction.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent for the mutation choice; tolerance outcomes measured in this study (Figure 5).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Mutation sites were directly transferred from published DERA stabilization studies.
